paper_b.title: Mice with finitely many Woodin cardinals from optimal determinacy hypotheses

metadata.description: Two set-theoretic foundational programs operating on disjoint corners of the subject. Shelah develops PCF / pseudopower theory to bound singular cardinal arithmetic in ZFC alone (no large-cardinal hypotheses); Muller-Schindler-Woodin work in inner-model theory, deriving the existence and iterability of mice with finitely many Woodin cardinals from optimal projective determinacy hypotheses. Both papers share the broad set-theoretic vocabulary (cardinals, cofinality, ultrafilters/iteration, large cardinals) but their main objects (pcf, pp, covering numbers vs $M_n^\#$, Q-structures, iteration trees, projective determinacy) are non-overlapping research programs aimed at different parts of the universe of sets. Almost every paper-original Level-1 contribution on each side has no counterpart on the other; the only contentful cross-paper matches are in the shared classical background (cofinality, large cardinals as obstructions/hypotheses).

matches.explanation: Shelah's explicit Definition of cofinality (and the regular/singular dichotomy) is a classical background notion both papers tacitly use, but paper 407 does not introduce its own cofinality definition node — cofinality there is invoked only through specific objects ($\omega_1$, $\omega_2$, Woodin $\delta$, etc.). The classical-vs-classical citation is uninformative for the pair so we leave it unmatched.

Strong limit cardinal — classical background used by Shelah's cardinal-arithmetic bounds (e.g. Theorem A on $2^{\aleph_\omega}$). No counterpart node in paper 407, whose interest is in Woodin cardinals / projective hierarchy rather than continuum-function bounds.

Filter / reduced product / ultrafilter / ultraproduct are foundational tools in Shelah's pcf machinery. Paper 407 uses extender sequences and iteration trees rather than ultraproducts; while extenders generalize measures (which are ultrafilters), no node in 407 corresponds at the granularity of these classical definitions.
Closed-unbounded filter $\FF_\alpha$ — used in Shelah's representation theorems. No matching closed-unbounded-filter node on the inner-model-theory side; club-set use in 407 is implicit.

Possible cofinality, $\pcf\bfa$, true cofinality $\tcf$ — the defining notions of Shelah's PCF program. There is no counterpart in paper 407; PCF objects are simply not part of the Muller-Schindler-Woodin program.
Pseudopower $\pp_\kappa(\lambda)$ and the auxiliary set $\PP_\kappa(\lambda)$ — Shelah-original technology, central to bounding $2^{\aleph_\omega}$. No counterpart in paper 407.

$\kappa$-inaccessible cardinal as defined by Shelah ($\mu^\kappa<\lambda$) — a hypothesis used in the pseudopower bounds. Paper 407 uses inaccessibility (e.g. TP407.14 about $\omega_2$ strongly inaccessible in HOD) but in a fundamentally different sense and within its own model-theoretic context. We mark `none` rather than analogous because the two notions of inaccessibility play disjoint roles.

Covering and weak covering numbers $\cov(\lambda,\kappa)$ — core to Shelah's covering-vs-pp results. Paper 407 invokes weak-covering-style arguments inside the proof of Steel's proper-class theorem (case 1 of PP407.3) but does not extract them as named nodes; no Level-1 counterpart exists.
Index of a cardinal — bookkeeping notation specific to Shelah's $\aleph$-arithmetic. No node in paper 407.

Boolean order algebra, $\lambda$-narrow, entangled linear order — combinatorial objects used in the applications section of Shelah's paper (Theorems 9.5, 9.6). No counterpart in the inner-model-theory paper.
Jónsson algebra — classical algebraic object Shelah builds at $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ as an application. No counterpart in paper 407.

Theorems A and A' — Shelah's headline ZFC bounds on $2^{\aleph_\omega}$ and $\aleph_\omega^{\aleph_0}$. Paper 407 does not produce or address such cardinal-arithmetic bounds; its main results (TP407.10, CP407.2) are equivalences between projective determinacy and existence of mice.
Theorem B' (4.2): $\aleph_\omega^{\aleph_0} < \aleph_{(2^{\aleph_0})^+}$. Cited Shelah result with no MSW counterpart.
Main theorem on pcf structure (4.3) — the structural bedrock of pcf theory ($|\pcf\bfa|\le 2^{|\bfa|}$, max exists, generators). Has no analogue in paper 407.
Localization Theorem (4.4) — pcf-theoretic closure result. No counterpart in 407.
Theorem 5.2: pseudopower bounds $\pp_\kappa(\lambda)\le\lambda^\kappa$ (with equality under inaccessibility). No counterpart in 407.
Convexity Theorem (5.3) — pcf structure. No counterpart in 407.
First and Second Representation Theorems (5.4, 5.5) — produce specific true-cofinality witnesses inside reduced products. No counterpart in 407.
$\pp_\kappa(\lambda)=\cov(\lambda,\kappa)$ and the weak-covering and stationary-equality theorems (5.7-5.9). Pure pcf/covering content; no counterpart in paper 407.

$\pp(\aleph_\omega) < \aleph_{\omega_4}$, the global $\pp$ bound for $\aleph_{\alpha+\delta}$, and the cofinality of $\langle S_{\le\aleph_0}(\aleph_{\omega_4}); \subseteq\rangle$ — Shelah's chief cardinal-arithmetic outputs. Inner-model-theoretic paper 407 has no comparable bounds.

Shelah's Corollary 7.1 says large $\pp(\lambda)$ rules out making $\kappa$ supercompact in any extension — a non-existence result about (super)compact large cardinals. Paper 407's Definition 4 introduces Woodin cardinals as the *positive* large-cardinal hypothesis underlying its determinacy program. The match is `analogous` (both center on large cardinals, in opposite roles: Shelah constrains them, MSW use them as primitive) and confidence is `low` because they sit at very different levels of the large-cardinal hierarchy and play opposite logical roles. We list it to flag the only thematic overlap on large cardinals.
Lemmas 7.2-7.4 (pp via covering at cofinality $\aleph_0$; large pp implies many fixed points; pp equals $\lambda^\kappa$ on a club) — pcf-internal lemmas. No counterpart in 407.
Consequences of the Strong / Weak Hypotheses on $\pp$. No analogue in paper 407.
Strong and Weak Hypotheses ($\pp(\lambda)=\lambda^+$ etc.) — pcf-axiomatic conjectures. No paper 407 analogue.
Theorem 9.1 (model-theoretic $L_{\infty,\lambda}$-equivalence). No counterpart in 407.

Shelah's combinatorial applications (Jónsson algebra at $\aleph_{\omega+1}$, chain conditions, coloring, narrow Boolean algebras, almost-disjoint and almost-free abelian groups). All are downstream of pcf theory and have no inner-model-theoretic counterpart.
Proof of Theorem 6.3 (the global $\pp$ bound) using Convexity, Localization, Second Representation. Pure pcf-theoretic argument with no counterpart proof in 407.
$n$-small premouse, $M_n^\#(x)$, $M_n(x)$, $M_n^\#(N)$ — the central premouse hierarchy of MSW. Shelah's paper does not work with mice, fine extender sequences, or $\omega_1$-iterability.
$\mathcal{Q}$-structure for $\mathcal{T}$ and the $\mathcal{Q}$-structure iteration strategy. Inner-model-theoretic machinery with no counterpart in Shelah's pcf paper.
$\delta$ not definably Woodin over $M$ — local-Woodinness predicate used in iteration arguments. No Shelah counterpart.
Coding / OD-order / iterated $L[E]$ / equivalence $M\sim N$ — auxiliary inner-model definitions specific to the OD-determinacy and proper-class arguments. No Shelah counterpart.

Pre-$n$-suitable, short/maximal trees, short-tree iterability, $n$-suitable, lower-part model $Lp^n(A)$ — the suitability/iterability framework for the existence theorems in MSW. No counterpart in Shelah's paper.
Boldface determinacy from $M_n^\#$, lightface $M_n^\#$ existence, and the equivalence theorem — the headline results of MSW. No counterpart in Shelah's pcf paper.

Steel's proper-class model with $n$ Woodins and the $\omega_2$-strongly-inaccessible-in-HOD theorem. Proven within paper 407's program; no Shelah counterpart (the role of $\omega_2$ inside HOD is specific to descriptive-set-theoretic inner-model setting).
The odd-case and even-case existence theorems for $M_n^\#$ and the $\omega_2$-inaccessible-in-HOD analogue. Specific to the projective-hierarchy stratification of MSW.

Boldface relativized equivalence, boldface determinacy transfer, $\omega_1$ measurable in HOD, absoluteness of short-tree iterability, coiteration without definable Woodins, game-quantifier transfer. All are inner-model / determinacy outputs with no Shelah counterpart.
Correctness lemmas (incl. periodicity) for $M_n^\#$. No Shelah counterpart.
Kechris-Solovay generalization (OD-determinacy in $M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x$). No Shelah counterpart; OD-determinacy and the projective hierarchy are not part of pcf theory.

Iterability / comparison / Steel's Lemma 2.2 generalization / no-fake-Woodin / coiteration without definable Woodins / OD-set agreement / projectum lemma — fine structural inner-model-theoretic lemmas.
$\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_{n+2}$-sequences are countable from $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_{n+1}$ determinacy — descriptive-set-theoretic fact. No Shelah counterpart.

Suitability-existence chain (existence of pre-$n$-suitable, weak condensation, $\Pi^1$-definability of short-tree iterability, pre-$(2n+1)$-suitable is $(2n+1)$-suitable, collapse-correctness, lower-part well-defined, Lp = iterate). All inner-model-theoretic; no Shelah counterpart.

Proofs of correctness lemma, KS lemma, Steel's proper-class theorem, pre-suitable=suitable, and bfDetSeq — all paper-original Level-1 proofs in the inner-model-theoretic program. No proof-level counterpart in Shelah's pcf paper.

Lightface conjecture for $M_n^\#$ at $n>1$ — open problem specific to MSW's program. No counterpart Shelah open problem in this paper (Shelah's open questions, e.g. whether the $\aleph_{\omega_4}$ bound can be improved, are not extracted as nodes here).
